newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: KEY AUSTRALIAN SENATOR TO FACE COURT IN DECEMBER.
newsitem.headline: KEY AUSTRALIAN SENATOR TO FACE COURT IN DECEMBER.

text.p: Australian independent senator Mal Colston will face a committal hearing in December on fraud charges relating to his parliamentary entitlements.

Colston's committal hearing would start in the Australian Capital Territory's Magistrates Court on December 8, while a similar case against former Liberal senator Noel Crichton-Browne would be mentioned in court on September 2.
Crichton-Browne's lawyer, Ian Bradfield, asked for a mention date for September on the basis that the case was of some complexity and his client lived in Western Australia.
Neither Colston nor Crichton-Browne were in court on Tuesday for the initial mention of the charges against them.
The matters against both men concerned alleged abuses of travel allowance and frequent flyer points.
If convicted, Colston would have to resign from parliament, changing the balance of power to help the Labor opposition in the non-government dominated upper house Senate.
